archetype: Ranged single-target burst archer. Damage is concentrated in Snipe and its Empowered/Ultimate follow-ups rather than in a hold-to-fire main attack, with Piercing Arrow as the line-clear skill.

linkSkill.name: Adventurer's Curiosity
linkSkill.effect: At master level: Monster Collection add chance +50%, Critical Rate +15%, Damage +6% (the Damage component appears at Lv. 7). The wiki notes the bonus is multiplicative rather than additive. Stacks up to 3 times, once per unique Explorer Bowman job character on the world - so it is shared with Bow Master and Pathfinder, not exclusive to Marksman.

legionEffect.notes: NamuWiki's KMS page treats the class's own crit-rate union effect as combining with crit-rate legion picks specifically because of the Vicious Shot conversion (see gearingNotes).

priority.why: Ranked in the top tier by both the Grandis Library node table and the class's own quick-guide infographic, and named as the first skill of the main trio by an outside cross-class trio reference. Snipe is the class's single-target damage skill and its Empowered/Ultimate follow-ups scale with it.
Second top-tier node in the Grandis table and second skill of the main trio in both the class infographic and the independent trio reference.

Third slot of the main trio. The class infographic pairs Bolt Burst with Frostprey in one node; the independent trio reference lists Bolt Burst as the third main-trio skill. Grandis's own table places this pair one tier below Snipe and Piercing Arrow.

priority.node: High Speed Shot / Arrow Illusion, Final Attack: Crossbow (secondary boost nodes)
priority.why: Both the class infographic and the independent trio reference put High Speed Shot and Final Attack: Crossbow in the second trio. Grandis groups Final Attack: Crossbow with High Speed Shot as one node in its second tier.

The class quick-guide infographic fills the third slot of the secondary trio with Covering Fire but marks it as not worth building. The independent trio reference also lists it as the third skill of the second trio, without comment. Grandis places Covering Fire in its lowest tier.

The class quick-guide infographic calls Split Shot the most important skill node for both bossing and levelling and marks it very high priority. The skill's own description supports why: while Split Shot is active, landing Full Burst Shot after Piercing Arrow, Snipe, either Empowered variant, Ultimate Piercing, Ultimate Snipe, HEXA High Speed Shot, Final Aim or Repeating Crossbow Cartridge causes the arrow to split for extra hits, so it multiplies the rest of the kit rather than adding damage on its own.

trios.notes: Two lanes that do not share an author agree on these three skills: the Marksman Discord's own quick-guide infographic and mastermysty's cross-class trio table. The infographic writes the first two as Snipe/Empowered Snipe and Piercing Arrow/Empowered Piercing Arrow, i.e. the boost node covers the Empowered versions too.

skills: High Speed Shot (paired with Arrow Illusion)
trios.notes: The two sources agree on the three skills. They disagree slightly on pairing: the infographic pairs High Speed Shot with Arrow Illusion, while Grandis's node table pairs High Speed Shot with Final Attack: Crossbow in one node and puts Covering Fire with Swift Surge in a lower tier.

vMatrix.notes: No public Marksman class document exists. Grandis Library's per-class pages normally carry a 'Class Doc' link; the Marksman page has none, and its credits attribute the inner ability, hyper passive and boost node fields to the Marksman Discord directly. So the Grandis page and the Grandis-hosted infographics are ONE source family, not two. The only genuinely outside corroboration found for trios is mastermysty's cross-class table, which self-reports a 2024-11-21 page date and 2024-05-14 data - that predates the v.269 boost-node regrouping (Grandis exposes a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle, which is direct evidence the groupings changed). Treat the agreement on WHICH three skills matter as solid, and the exact node pairings as needing a re-check against the Discord. No source found states a node levelling order (which trio skill to push to 60 first).

order.step: Open several different nodes at level 1 before deep-levelling any one of them
order.why: Both of the class's published 6th-job charts begin with a run of level-1 entries (the fragment-efficient chart's first five entries are all Lv 1) before any entry asks for a higher target level.
order.caveat: Read from the level labels on the charts, which are legible. The identity of each node icon was NOT resolved and is deliberately not recorded here.

order.step: HEXA Stat cores are activated part-way through the sequence, not at the start
order.why: In the fragment-efficient chart the three HEXA Stat entries (labelled Stat 1, Stat 2, Stat 3) appear at roughly the 36th, 49th and 61st entries of a chart of about 170 entries - i.e. after a substantial block of skill, mastery and boost investment.
order.caveat: The Stat 1/2/3 labels are legible; the entry numbers assume the chart is read left to right, row by row, across its 13-column grid. Treat the positions as approximate.

mechanicalNotes.claim: HEXA Piercing Arrow carries a passive that permanently enhances HEXA Snipe, and the bonus grows sharply with its level.
mechanicalNotes.why: The skill's own passive effect line lists added damage to HEXA Snipe, Empowered Snipe and Ultimate Snipe, rising from a few percentage points at Lv. 1 to the 60-132 percentage point range at Lv. 30. That is a real coupling between two mastery nodes, which is the kind of thing an investment order gets built around - but no source found states what order to build them in, so none is recorded.

mechanicalNotes.claim: HEXA Enhancement (boost) final damage rises linearly per level with jumps at levels 10, 20 and 30.
mechanicalNotes.why: Stated on the wiki's Marksman HEXA Enhancements section. The two class skill cores also list their own breakpoint bonuses at Lv. 10/20/30 (Final Aim: Ignore DEF and Boss Damage; Fatal Trigger: Ignore DEF and Boss Damage).

hexa.notes: THE PER-NODE HEXA ORDER FOR MARKSMAN IS PUBLISHED ONLY AS IMAGES AND IS NOT TRANSCRIBED HERE. Grandis Library hosts two Marksman 6th-job charts, credited to the Marksman Discord and last checked 2026-06-25: 'Fragments Efficient' (https://grandislibrary.com/class-infographic/marksman/marksman-6th-job-fragments.png) and 'Energy Efficient' (https://grandislibrary.com/class-infographic/marksman/marksman-6th-job-energy.png). Each is a grid of skill icons with a target level under each, giving a full upgrade-by-upgrade sequence. The level labels are readable; the individual node icons were not identified to a confidence level that would justify writing node names down, so no order is claimed. Surface the images to the user rather than a transcription. The fragment-efficient variant is the one that matters for GMS Heroic, where Sol Erda Fragments are the binding constraint. Nothing outside the Marksman Discord family publishes any Marksman HEXA order - there is no class doc, mapledoro's 6th-job section reads 'Coming soon', and the aggregator sites carry no Marksman-specific ordering.

hyperStats.notes: No source was found that states a Marksman hyper stat priority order. Grandis Library carries no hyper stat section for any class; the Marksman quick-guide infographic has no hyper stat block; mapledoro's Marksman page has none; and there is no Marksman class document. Nothing is recorded here rather than importing another class's list. The community's operative answer to hyper stat allocation is a per-character computation against a given boss rather than a fixed list - MathBro's hyper stat optimizer at https://brendonmay.github.io/hyperCalculator/ - which is a cross-class fact, not a Marksman-specific one. One Marksman-specific input to that calculation IS recorded, under gearingNotes: because of Vicious Shot, critical rate does not stop paying at 100%, so any optimizer or planner that hard-caps crit at 100% will under-rate the crit rate hyper stat for this class.

bossing.notes: The infographic and the Grandis page table are the same source family (both credited to the Marksman Discord) and they agree. Grandis's bossing table lists Sharp Eyes - Guardbreak, Sharp Eyes - Critical Chance and the three Snipe lines, matching the infographic.

passives: Snipe - Reinforce OR Sharp Eyes - Critical Chance
training.notes: The infographic gives the fifth pick as a choice between Snipe - Reinforce and Sharp Eyes - Critical Chance. Grandis's training table lists the three Piercing Arrow lines plus Snipe - Extra Strike and Snipe - Reinforce.

hyperSkills.notes: No source found states which hyper actives to take. The three available are Bullseye Shot, High Speed Shot and Epic Adventure (maplestorywiki). High Speed Shot doubles as a boost-node and HEXA mastery target, so it is unlikely to be optional in practice, but no source says so - left unclaimed.

lines.why: Stated as the first line by the class quick-guide infographic and listed first on the Grandis page. An independent cross-class source supports the shape of the recommendation: maplestorywiki's inner ability guide gives Attack Speed as the top-line rule for Explorer classes that do not have a Hurricane-type skill, and Marksman's skill list contains no such skill (unlike Bow Master, which has Hurricane and is steered toward Boss Damage instead).

Second line in the class infographic. NamuWiki's KMS page reaches the same conclusion by an independent route, citing the Vicious Shot conversion as the reason crit rate keeps paying for this class, and placing the line in the second or third slot.
Third line in the class infographic and third entry on the Grandis page.

alternatives.line: Damage to enemies with an abnormal status (Unique, up to 8%)
alternatives.why: NamuWiki's KMS page ranks this second among the lines to chase, after boss damage.

alternatives.line: Meso obtained / item drop rate, and damage to normal monsters, on a separate training preset
alternatives.why: NamuWiki's KMS page describes keeping these on a hunting preset and swapping on reward maps. This matches the cross-class pattern in maplestorywiki's inner ability guide of running a distinct training preset.

innerAbility.notes: Grandis Library normally splits recommended inner ability into bossing and training and labels it by attack-speed-cap region; the Marksman page does not - it carries a single flat list of three lines. The line ORDER recorded above comes from the quick-guide infographic, which explicitly labels them 1st / 2nd / 3rd line. See conflicts for the GMS-vs-KMS disagreement on the top line.

gearingNotes:
CRITICAL RATE DOES NOT STOP PAYING AT 100%. Vicious Shot, the shared Explorer Archer 5th job skill, allows Critical Rate to exceed 100% and increases Critical Damage by a percentage of total Critical Rate - 21% of crit rate at Lv. 1 rising to 50% at Lv. 30 - for 30 seconds on a 120 second cooldown (the skill's own additional crit rate is excluded from the conversion). Source: maplestorywiki's Marksman skill page. NamuWiki's KMS page reaches the same practical conclusion independently, treating crit-rate inner ability lines and the crit-rate union/legion picks as valuable specifically because they convert during that window. Consequence for a planner: do not hard-cap crit rate at 100% for this class, and do not rank the crit rate hyper stat or the crit-rate inner ability line the way you would for a class that caps. NOTE THIS IS NOT A MARKSMAN-VS-BOW-MASTER DIFFERENCE - Vicious Shot is shared by both Explorer Archers, and the Bow Master entry records the same quirk. [sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills ; https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EA%B6%81(%EB%A9%94%EC%9D%B4%ED%94%8C%EC%8A%A4%ED%86%A0%EB%A6%AC)]

MARKSMAN ARRIVES AT HIGH CRIT RATE LARGELY ON ITS OWN. Grandis Library's base-stats-from-skills summary for Marksman totals +75% Critical Rate from passives and buffs before gear, links or legion. Contributing skills on the wiki include Critical Shot (+40% at max), Sharp Eyes (+20%, plus +5% from the Sharp Eyes - Critical Chance hyper passive), Bullseye Shot (+20% for its duration) and the class's own link skill (+15%, which the wiki notes applies multiplicatively). Snipe, Perfect Shot and Surge Bolt additionally carry +100% bonus critical rate on their own hits, and Evasion Boost makes attacks in the second after a successful dodge critical. This is why crit rate reads as a mid-priority line rather than a starving one - the payoff is the Vicious Shot conversion, not reaching the cap. [sources: https://grandislibrary.com/explorers/marksman ; https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills]

A CLASS MECHANIC THAT CHANGES SETUP RATHER THAN GEAR: Perfect Shot (KMS name True Sniping) is aimed with the mouse - the skill description instructs the player to attack with the left mouse button and cancel with the right. NamuWiki's KMS page calls this out as a mechanism unique to Marksman among all classes, in a game otherwise played from the keyboard during boss fights. Worth surfacing to a player coming from Bow Master. [sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills ; https://en.namu.wiki/w/%EC%8B%A0%EA%B6%81(%EB%A9%94%EC%9D%B4%ED%94%8C%EC%8A%A4%ED%86%A0%EB%A6%AC)]

NO SOURCE WAS FOUND on Marksman weapon/secondary/emblem potential lines, IED targets, or boss damage targets. The Bow Master class document covers those for its class; Marksman has no equivalent document, so those fields are left unwritten rather than carried across from Bow Master.

commonMistakes.mistake: Firing the big burst skills without Split Shot running.
commonMistakes.why: Split Shot's own description makes Full Burst Shot split into extra arrows only while Split Shot is active, and the list of skills it triggers off includes Final Aim (the Origin skill) and Repeating Crossbow Cartridge. NamuWiki's KMS page states the damage difference with and without Split Shot is large even for those burst skills, and the class quick-guide infographic independently flags Split Shot as the highest-priority skill node for both bossing and levelling.

commonMistakes.mistake: Sinking nodestone rolls into Covering Fire.
commonMistakes.why: The class quick-guide infographic lists Covering Fire only as the filler third slot of the secondary trio and marks it as not worth building; Grandis's node table places it in its lowest tier.

differencesFromBowMaster.detail: Marksman's main trio is Snipe / Piercing Arrow / Bolt Burst; the same cross-class reference gives Bow Master's as Hurricane / Arrow Blaster / Quiver Cartridge. No skill overlaps between the two main trios.

Marksman's own recommendation puts Attack Speed +1 first; the Bow Master entry in this dataset records Boss Damage +20% first. maplestorywiki's cross-class inner ability guide gives the rule that predicts the split - Attack Speed for Explorer classes without a Hurricane-type skill, Boss Damage for burst-focused classes. Bow Master has Hurricane; Marksman does not.

differencesFromBowMaster.claim: The crit-past-cap quirk is NOT a difference.
differencesFromBowMaster.detail: Vicious Shot is shared by both Explorer Archers, so the 'keep buying crit rate past 100%' advice applies identically to Marksman.

differencesFromBowMaster.claim: Sourcing quality is much worse for Marksman.
differencesFromBowMaster.detail: Bow Master has a maintained class document (Book of Bowmaster) and an independently written Dexless guide. Marksman has no public class document at all - Grandis Library's Marksman page carries no 'Class Doc' link, unlike its Bow Master page, and credits its judgement fields to the Marksman Discord directly. Every piece of Marksman node, HEXA and inner ability judgement traces to one Discord. Present Marksman advice with visibly lower confidence than Bow Master advice.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
defects: THE BOOST NODE TIERS ARE REPORTED BACKWARDS. The Grandis Marksman page's own page data reads "primary":[0,1,2,3],"secondary":[4,5] - Nodes 1-4 are PRIMARY (Snipe; Piercing Arrow; Bolt Burst+Frostprey; Final Attack: Crossbow+High Speed Shot), Nodes 5-6 are SECONDARY (Covering Fire+Swift Surge; Arrow Blow+Arrow Illusion), and the OTHER tier is empty for Marksman. The file states in three places that Bolt Burst/Frostprey sits "one tier below Snipe and Piercing Arrow" (false - same tier), that Final Attack: Crossbow + High Speed Shot is in Grandis's "second tier" (false - Primary), and that Covering Fire is in "its lowest tier" (Secondary is the lower of two used tiers, but see next item). The error propagates into vMatrix entries 3, 4 and 5, trios[1].notes, commonMistakes[1], conflicts[1] and sources[0].

GRANDIS'S TIERS ARE NOT A DAMAGE-PRIORITY RANKING. The page's own Boost Node Legend defines PRIMARY as "Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used", SECONDARY as "Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used", OTHER as "do not need to be upgraded or has least priority", and states that "Nodes categorized as Primary and Secondary are recommended to be upgraded". The file treats the tiers as a priority ordering throughout. This also means Grandis's Primary set is exactly the set of nodes gating HEXA mastery cores 1-4 - a sourced rationale for node priority that the file missed entirely.

commonMistakes[1] ("Sinking nodestone rolls into Covering Fire") cites the Grandis page as supporting evidence, but Grandis puts Covering Fire in SECONDARY and explicitly says Primary and Secondary nodes are recommended to be upgraded. The Grandis citation contradicts the mistake rather than supporting it; the only remaining support is the infographic, which I could not read.

innerAbility.notes claims "Grandis Library normally splits recommended inner ability into bossing and training and labels it by attack-speed-cap region". No such region labelling exists. The Grandis inner-ability data structure carries only an optional name field, used as "For Bossing" / "For Training" (verified on the Bow Master page); there is no region or attack-speed-cap field anywhere in the schema or on either page. This invented convention is the sole basis for the conflicts[0] note's "likely a region artefact" explanation of the contested top line, so that explanation has no support. The other half of the sentence - that Grandis normally splits bossing/training and the Marksman page does not - is correct.

innerAbility.alternatives[0].why says NamuWiki "ranks this second among the lines to chase, after boss damage". The page says the opposite reference point: abnormal-status damage is lower in importance than crit rate and is therefore targeted as the 2nd priority AFTER CRIT RATE ("lower importance than crit rate, so it is targeted second after crit rate"). Boss damage is not the anchor.

gearingNotes glosses the Vicious Shot exclusion as "(the skill's own additional crit rate is excluded from the conversion)". Vicious Shot grants no crit rate of its own. The wiki line "The attack's additional Critical Rate is not applied" means per-attack Bonus Critical Rate - Snipe, Perfect Shot, Surge Bolt and Greater Empowered Arrows each carry Bonus Critical Rate: 100% - does not feed the conversion. This matters for a planner: the conversion runs off the character's actual crit-rate stat, which strengthens the file's conclusion but for a different mechanism than the one written down.

sources[9] claims MapleDoro's inner ability is "character-for-character identical to the Grandis / Marksman Discord list (Attack Speed +1 / Crit Rate +20% / Boss Damage +10%)". MapleDoro actually lists two lines - Legendary Attack Speed +1 and Unique Crit Rate +20% - and splits them across Bossing and Mobbing. No Boss Damage +10% line. The conclusion (rule it out as a corroborating source) may still be right; the evidence given for it is not.

sources[4] characterises mystyjl as "backed by the author's own trio-probability testing, so it is a genuine second opinion on trios". The page's only stated methodology is the odds of FINDING all trios within 200 nodes (10,000 simulations per class, dated May 14th 2024). It states no provenance whatsoever for which skills belong in each trio, and invites corrections by DM. Probability-of-finding testing is not evidence about trio selection, so the claim of an independent second opinion is unsupported - the trio lists may well descend from the same class Discords.
sources[0] describes the Grandis node table as "six two-skill nodes". Nodes 1 and 2 are single-skill (Snipe alone; Piercing Arrow alone); only nodes 3-6 pair two skills.
clearedOnInspection: NO fabricated skill or node names were found. Every name in the file checks out against maplestorywiki.net/w/Marksman/Skills and/or the Grandis node table: Bolt Burst (3rd job), Frostprey (3rd job), Covering Fire (2nd job), Swift Surge (2nd job), Arrow Blow (1st job), Arrow Illusion (4th job), Final Attack: Crossbow (2nd job), High Speed Shot (hyper active, Lv 160), Split Shot, Perfect Shot, Surge Bolt, Repeating Crossbow Cartridge, Vicious Shot, Final Aim (Origin), Fatal Trigger (Ascent), the six HEXA mastery names, and the four HEXA Enhancement boosts. The hyper passive and hyper active lists, the link skill values (MC +50% / Crit +15% / Damage +6% at Lv 9, multiplicative, stacks 3, Damage component at Lv 7), Vicious Shot 21%->50%, the Split Shot trigger list, the HEXA Piercing Arrow -> HEXA Snipe passive (+60 to +132 percentage points at Lv 30), Grandis's +75% crit from skills, and the legion crit 1/2/3/4/5% all match their cited sources exactly. What follows are asserted claims contradicted by, or absent from, the sources cited for them.
